宇都宮餃子.summary: Utsunomiya is known, along with Hamamatsu, as one of Japan's gyoza cities. It is said that gyoza spread here after the war, brought by people returning from Manchuria. The city has many specialist shops, and besides pan-fried gyoza, boiled and deep-fried versions are popular at some. Many shops use a light, vegetable-rich filling, and they are eaten with vinegar and chili oil. There is even a gyoza statue in front of the station, and many visitors go on gyoza tours. Frozen gyoza to take home are popular too.

shops.name: Utsunomiya Minmin Main Store
shops.query: 宇都宮みんみん 本店
shops.comment: The best-known Utsunomiya gyoza shop, on Gyoza Street.
shops.access: Gyoza Street (about 5 min walk from Utsunomiya Station)

shops.name: Masashi Miyajimacho
shops.query: 正嗣 宮島町店
shops.comment: A veteran shop serving only fried and boiled gyoza. Often has a line.

佐野ラーメン.summary: The local ramen of Sano. Its hand-made noodles are rolled out with a green bamboo pole, a technique called aotake-uchi, making them flat, soft yet springy. The clear, light soy sauce broth made from chicken bones goes perfectly with the noodles. There are many ramen shops in the city, and quite a few have long lines. Combine it with a visit to Sano Yakuyoke Daishi temple or shopping at the outlet mall. Its gentle, old-fashioned flavor and the texture of the noodles are the draw.

shops.name: Moritaya Sohonten
shops.query: 森田屋総本店 佐野
shops.comment: A shop in the original line of Sano ramen, running for over 60 years.

shops.name: Hinataya
shops.query: 青竹手打ラーメン 日向屋 佐野
shops.comment: Popular for chewy noodles kneaded with bamboo poles.

いもフライ.summary: A local favorite in Sano: steamed potatoes on a skewer, battered and deep-fried, then drizzled with plenty of sweet sauce. The combination of fluffy potato, crispy coating and sauce is simple yet addictive. They are sold at specialist shops, butchers and festival stalls in the city, and are cheap and easy to enjoy. Along with Sano ramen, they are a soul food loved by locals for many years. Try them fresh from the fryer.

shops.name: Idei Yakisobaten
shops.query: いでい焼そば店 佐野
shops.comment: A long-running imo-fry shop using Hokkaido danshaku potatoes.

shops.name: Imofry Okamoto
shops.query: いもフライ 岡本 佐野
shops.comment: A popular imo-fry shop that also does takeout.

那須塩原スープ入り焼きそば.summary: A local dish born in the Kuroiso district of Nasushiobara: yakisoba with soy sauce soup poured over it. Because the sauce-fried noodles are served in soup, the sauce and broth blend into a unique flavor somewhere between yakisoba and ramen. It began as the specialty of a local diner and is now served at many restaurants in the city. Each shop's soup and toppings differ, so comparing them is fun. Stop by on a trip to the Nasu highlands or Shiobara Onsen. There is nothing else quite like it.

shops.name: Kamahiko
shops.query: 釜彦 塩原 スープ入り焼きそば
shops.comment: One of the original shops for soup yakisoba. Lunch only.

shops.name: Kobaya Shokudo
shops.query: こばや食堂 塩原
shops.comment: A diner in Shiobara Onsen for about 60 years, often with a line.

しもつかれ.summary: A traditional dish from northern Kanto, centered on Tochigi. Salmon heads, coarsely grated daikon and carrot, roasted soybeans, fried tofu and sake lees are simmered together. It is made on the first Day of the Horse in February and offered at Inari shrines, and it is said that eating shimotsukare from seven different homes keeps illness away. It looks unusual, but the richness of sake lees and the umami of salmon make for a simple, nourishing flavor. It appears in supermarkets at this time of year.

shops.name: Michi no Eki Shimotsuke
shops.query: 道の駅しもつけ
shops.comment: Its deli corner stocks shimotsukare and other local dishes.

shops.name: Michi no Eki Domannaka Tanuma
shops.query: 道の駅 どまんなかたぬま
shops.comment: A roadside station with plenty of local foods, including shimotsukare.

耳うどん.summary: Ear-shaped udon from areas such as Senba in the former town of Kuzu, Sano. Square pieces of wheat dough are folded into the shape of an ear. It is eaten at New Year, and legend says that eating the ears of evil spirits stops them from hearing your family's affairs that year. It is simmered with vegetables in a soy-based dashi soup and has a unique chewy texture. You can try it at restaurants in the city. It is also loved as a dish that brings good luck.

shops.name: Nomuraya Honten
shops.query: 野村屋本店 佐野 耳うどん
shops.comment: Founded in the Meiji era; the go-to shop for mimi udon.
shops.access: About 8 min walk from Sano Station

shops.name: Tochinoki (Sano SA, northbound)
shops.query: 佐野サービスエリア 下り 栃乃木
shops.comment: Try mimi udon casually at the expressway service area.

揚げまき湯波の煮物.summary: Nikko's famous yuba (tofu skin) rolled up, deep-fried and simmered in a sweet and savory broth. In Nikko, yuba is usually written with characters different from Kyoto's. While Kyoto yuba is thin, Nikko yuba is said to be lifted differently, making it thicker and more substantial. Frying adds richness, and it soaks up the broth to become wonderfully juicy. You can find it at long-established restaurants and inns in Nikko. It also has a history as part of Buddhist vegetarian cuisine, and its flavor is refined.

shops.name: Nikko Yuba Fujiya
shops.query: 日光湯波 ふじや
shops.comment: A yuba specialist founded in the Meiji era with dozens of kinds.

shops.name: Kappo Ebisuya
shops.query: 割烹 恵比寿家 日光
shops.comment: Serves courses using yuba from appetizer to dessert.

日光湯波そば.summary: Soba topped with Nikko's famous yuba (tofu skin). The gentle flavor of the yuba goes perfectly with the warm, dashi-rich broth. Nikko yuba is thick, keeping a satisfying texture even after soaking in the soup. It is a popular, easy way to taste yuba between visits to World Heritage shrines and temples such as Toshogu and Rinnoji. You can try it at soba restaurants in Nikko. Hot soba is especially welcome in the cold season, and some shops serve it cold too.

shops.name: Yuba Soba Nikko Momijian
shops.query: ゆばそば 日光もみぢ庵
shops.comment: A shop specializing in yuba soba and yuba sushi.

shops.name: Soba-dokoro Hayashiya
shops.query: そば処 林屋 日光
shops.comment: Handmade soba and Nikko's famous yuba.
shops.access: About 5 min walk from Nikko Toshogu

レモン牛乳.summary: A sweet, lemon-colored milk drink long loved in Tochigi. Despite the name, it has a gentle sweetness with a refreshing lemon flavor. For Tochigi people it is a nostalgic drink from childhood, sometimes called the prefecture's soul drink. It is easy to buy at supermarkets and convenience stores in the prefecture, and there are many related products such as lemon milk sweets and ice cream. Try it at least once when you visit Tochigi; it is perfect after a hot spring bath too.

shops.name: Utsunomiya Paseo (station)
shops.query: 宇都宮パセオ
shops.comment: A shopping area inside Utsunomiya Station where you can buy lemon milk.

shops.name: Michi no Eki Utsunomiya Romantic Mura
shops.query: 道の駅うつのみや ろまんちっく村
shops.comment: A roadside station stocked with Tochigi products.

とちおとめジェラート.summary: Tochigi has long been Japan's top strawberry producer. Gelato made with Tochiotome, the prefecture's signature variety, offers the sweet-tart aroma of strawberries and a smooth, melting texture. You can find it at roadside stations, tourist farms and strawberry farm shops. During the strawberry-picking season from winter to spring, enjoy it alongside other strawberry sweets. In dairy areas like Nasu, you can also taste the richness of local milk. A perfect break during your travels.

shops.name: Michi no Eki Motegi
shops.query: 道の駅もてぎ おとめミルク
shops.comment: Famous for otome milk made with freshly picked strawberries. Available about November to May.

shops.name: Michi no Eki Ninomiya
shops.query: 道の駅にのみや
shops.comment: A roadside station in strawberry country, popular for its strawberry gelato.

御用邸チーズケーキ.summary: A popular Nasu sweet, a cheesecake named after the Imperial villa (goyotei) in Nasu. It has a rich cheese flavor and a moist, melt-in-the-mouth texture. At the shop in the Nasu highlands, you can also enjoy a variety of other cheese sweets. It is a very popular souvenir and can also be bought at highway service areas and stations. Stop by during a drive through the Nasu highlands for a fresh one. It is delicious chilled or slightly warmed, and makes a lovely gift.

shops.name: Cheese Garden Nasu Main Store
shops.query: チーズガーデン 那須本店
shops.comment: The main store with the widest selection, plus a cafe.

shops.name: Cheese Garden Tochigi Grand Marche
shops.query: チーズガーデン とちぎグランマルシェ店
shops.comment: Right by the ticket gates of Utsunomiya Station.

日光羊羹.summary: Yokan, sweet bean jelly made with Nikko's pure water. Many traditional yokan shops still remain in Nikko. It is said to have spread in the Edo period as a souvenir for pilgrims visiting Toshogu Shrine. Besides rich neri yokan that highlights the flavor of red beans, the lighter mizu yokan is also popular. Each shop's sweetness and texture differ, so comparing them is fun. It keeps well, making it a good souvenir for people far away, and it goes perfectly with green tea.

shops.name: Watahan Main Store
shops.query: 綿半 本店 日光
shops.comment: A yokan maker founded in the Edo period, famous for bamboo-wrapped yokan.

shops.name: Hishiya
shops.query: ひしや 日光 羊羹
shops.comment: A veteran maker of only neri-yokan; often sold out before noon.
